title: OPA Data Filtering
subtitle: Partial evaluation: decisions compiled to WHERE clauses
content:
🔽 From Decisions to Filters

Per-row PDP calls don't scale to analytics tables — and the warehouse can't call your sidecar per row. Partial evaluation compiles policy + known input into a residual query (e.g. SQL WHERE) the database enforces itself. Unknowns (row fields) stay symbolic; knowns (the requester's attributes) fold into constants. Verified against the OPA filtering docs:

Partial eval: knowns fold, unknowns become SQL 
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs OPA docs /filtering + REST /v1/compile
# METADATA
# scope: package
# compile:
#   unknowns: [input.employees]
package filters

include if {
    input.user.role == "director"                        # known -> consumed
    input.employees.department == input.user.department  # unknown == known -> SQL
}

# POST /v1/compile/filters/include  {"input": {"user": {...director, engineering...}}}
# Enterprise OPA SQL shape: { "result": { "query": "WHERE employees.department = 'engineering'" } }
# OSS OPA 1.8 shape:        { "result": {"queries": [...], "support": [...] } }  (Rego AST + translator)
# The app appends the filter: SELECT name, salary FROM employees $FILTER;
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs OPA docs /filtering + REST /v1/compile # METADATA # scope: package # compile: # unknowns: [input.employees] package filters include if { input.user.role == "director" # known -> consumed input.employees.department == input.user.department # unknown == known -> SQL } # POST /v1/compile/filters/include {"input": {"user": {...director, engineering...}}} # Enterprise OPA SQL shape: { "result": { "query": "WHERE employees.department = 'engineering'" } } # OSS OPA 1.8 shape: { "result": {"queries": [...], "support": [...] } } (Rego AST + translator) # The app appends the filter: SELECT name, salary FROM employees $FILTER;

🧪 The Two-User Proof (Docs Tutorial Shape)

Alice (director, engineering) compiles to WHERE department = engineering; Dave (director, marketing) compiles to WHERE department = marketing. Same policy, different filters — the requester's attributes specialize the query. This is ABAC executed by the database, and it is also why input correctness matters twice: a wrong department folds into a wrong filter silently. Lab note: add 30m if running the Postgres lab end-to-end.

🎭 Masking at Compile Time (Enterprise API)

Scope this precisely: on Enterprise OPA, the expanded compile API accepts a maskRule and can return SQL-shaped {"result": {"query": "..."}} — columns the policy masks become projections, not just filters. On OSS OPA 1.8 (pinned in this course), /v1/compile returns {"result": {"queries": [...], "support": ...}} — a Rego AST your translator turns into SQL. Filters decide which rows; masks decide which columns — the Immuta split (Lesson 17) reproduced inside OPA's compiler.

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • Residual queries need review like policies: a compiled WHERE true (over-permissive unknowns) is a breach in SQL clothing. Log compiled filters, sample them, alert on tautologies (e.g. alert when query LIKE '%WHERE 1=1%' OR query LIKE '%WHERE true%' OR query NOT LIKE '%WHERE%').
  • Translators are unsound until reviewed: OSS /v1/compile returns a Rego AST — your translator turns it into SQL. Never string-concat raw attribute values into SQL (injection); use bound parameters. Review the translator like policy code.
  • Not every rule compiles: rules with side effects, iteration over unknowns, or non-relational logic may refuse partial eval. Keep filter-path rules relational and simple; keep the exotic logic on the per-request path. Builtins that commonly break partial-eval: http.send, walk over unknowns, time/date arithmetic on unknowns, custom functions over unknowns — verify against OPA 1.8 filtering docs for your pinned version.
  • Freshness still applies: compiled filters embed the requester's attributes at compile time — recompile per request (or per attribute change), never cache across revocations.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Preview masking outcomes per role before implementing. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: Why compile policy to SQL instead of calling the PDP per row?

options.text: Per-row PDP calls don't scale; the database enforces the compiled filter itself
SQL is more secure by nature

questions.explanation: Bulk-data systems need answers shaped like queries (filters), not booleans — the same insight as PlainID Resolution.

questions.question: In the filters package, what do unknowns: [input.employees] declare?

options.text: Row fields stay symbolic (become SQL); requester attributes fold into constants

questions.explanation: Unknowns mark what the compiler cannot know yet. Knowns evaluate away; unknowns become the residual query.

questions.question: Alice (engineering) and Dave (marketing) compile the same policy. Result?

options.text: Different WHERE clauses specialized by each requester's attributes
An error — one policy, one filter

questions.explanation: Partial evaluation specializes: same policy plus different knowns yields different residual queries.

questions.question: What does the compile API's maskRule option produce?
questions.explanation: Filters gate rows, masks shape columns — the subscription/data split compiled into one artifact.

questions.question: A compiled filter reads WHERE true. Response?

options.text: Treat as a breach-shaped artifact: block, alert, fix the unknowns — never ship tautologies

questions.explanation: Over-permissive unknowns compile to allow-everything SQL. Residual queries get the same review gates as policies.

questions.question: A rule iterates over unknown rows with custom functions. Partial eval?

options.text: Likely refuses — keep filter-path rules relational and simple; exotic logic stays per-request

questions.explanation: Compilation has a supported fragment. Design filter-path rules for it; don't fight the compiler.

questions.question: Compiled filters embed requester attributes. Caching rule?

options.text: Recompile per request or attribute change — never cache across revocations
Cache one filter for all users

questions.explanation: A filter is a decision frozen with yesterday's attributes. Stale filters are stale verdicts.

questions.question: Which workload fits data filtering over per-request PDP calls?

options.text: Analytics tables and search indexes enforced by another system

questions.explanation: Bulk enforcement by foreign systems is the filtering lane; single decisions stay on the PDP hot path.
